name: NIST SP 800-22
description: The NIST SP 800-22 test suite serves as the benchmark for Random Number Generator (RNG) evaluation, yet default parameters frequently induce Type I errors due to approximation inaccuracies and Level-1 statistic sensitivity. This paper presents a systematic parameter optimization methodology designed to mitigate structural false rejections in the Frequency, Cumulative Sums, and Non-overlapping Template Matching tests. Analytical pass thresholds for the Frequency and Cumulative Sums tests are derived and aligned with statistically modeled maximum values to identify stable pass regions (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>). For the Non-overlapping Template Matching test, a parameter sweep based on sensitivity analysis is employed to determine the optimal (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n, N$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) set, effectively resolving hypersensitivity to strict decision boundaries. Experimental verification using a 28 nm
evaluation_method: pass/fail rates and p-value-based statistical testing
typical_sota_score: varies widely by generator; high-quality cryptographic/non-cryptographic RNGs typically exhibit >95% passing rates across many of the suite's statistical tests
reputation: A classic and widely used standard suite for evaluating the statistical randomness of RNGs and bitstreams.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results are highly sensitive to sample size, parameter settings, and multiple-testing effects, with known Type I error issues in default configurations.
